newsitem.title: USA: Lender says Massachusetts county defaults.
newsitem.headline: Lender says Massachusetts county defaults.

text.p: Boston Co. said Friday that Middlesex County, Mass., home to Harvard University and the Masssachusetts Institute of Technology, had defaulted on $3 million of notes that it owned and that were due on Friday.
"They were due today, so technically, that would be the case," said Vincent Loporchio, a spokesman for Boston Co., part of Mellon Bank Corp.
Fleet Financial Group said it expected to be informed Monday that the county had defaulted on $1.5 million of notes that the bank owns.

The Massachusetts Emergency Board on Friday decided not to allow the state's largest county, which runs from Cambridge, where both Harvard and MIT are located north to Lowell, to borrow funds to cover debt payments due the same day, a spokesman for the state attorney general said.
"The county came to the board to ask them to authorise borrowing. The board voted three to one against them," the spokesman said.

The emergency board turned down a request by the county to borrow about $6 million to repay the notes plus interest, saying that it wanted Middlesex to devise a long-term solution to its fiscal problems.

Middlesex ran into trouble with its county hospital which recently has been operating at just 25 percent capacity. It has agreed to sell the facility to for-profit Olympus Healthcare Group Inc. of Westborough, Mass. for $4.4 million, but that will not be enough to cover the county's $17 million in hospital associated liabilities.

The emergency board, set up by legislation in 1991, is composed of State Treasurer Joe Malone, Attorney General Scott Harshbarger and a representative from Gov. William Weld's Administration and Finance Department. This was its first meeting.
